# X36 – Ecosystem Integration, System Composition & End-to-End Compatibility

**Architecture-ID:** `ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X36-ECOSYSTEM-INTEGRATION-SYSTEM-COMPOSITION-END-TO-END-COMPATIBILITY`  
**Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`  
**Scope:** 17 sublayers · 170 planned function contracts

## Goal and architecture boundary

X36 defines how independent A-TownChain, GlobusOS and Aurora AI components compose into a coherent system without duplicating canonical implementations. It covers dependency contracts, end-to-end compatibility across APIs/data/events/runtime boundaries, cross-repository integration tests, compatibility matrices, reproducible evidence, failure isolation and safe degradation.

X32 owns API security/access mediation; X33 event governance and distributed workflows; X34 resource scheduling/capacity; X35 deployment/release/rollout governance. X36 composes and validates end-to-end behavior across those domains; it does not replace them.

**Principle:** Standalone First, Ecosystem Second. Components remain independently usable within their defined contracts; integration occurs only through explicit, documented contracts.

## Planned sublayers and contract ID ranges

All IDs below are proposed catalog/function-contract IDs, not claims that implementations exist.

| Sublayer | Planned IDs | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| X36.01 System Inventory & Component Composition | X36-001–010 | Component identity, canonical repository, manifests/capabilities, boundaries, composition profiles, duplicate detection, completeness, reproducible inventory |
| X36.02 Dependency Graph & Integration Constraints | X36-011–020 | Machine-readable dependencies, directed graph, cycles, version resolution, forbidden dependencies, optional/required integrations, unresolved dependencies, minimum viable profile, graph export |
| X36.03 Cross-Repository Contract Mapping | X36-021–030 | Contract-to-repository/path/symbol/full commit/blob mapping, provider-consumer comparison, missing/conflicting contracts, exceptions, cross-repo coverage and export |
| X36.04 Interface, Schema & Protocol Compatibility | X36-031–040 | API/schema/serialization/type/error/protocol compatibility, semantic changes, deprecation, backward/forward compatibility, compatibility matrix |
| X36.05 Data Model & State Interoperability | X36-041–050 | Shared models/IDs/units/timestamps, data ownership, state handoff, replicated-state conflicts, migrations, integrity/loss risks, data-contract catalog |
| X36.06 Identity, Capability & Trust Interoperability | X36-051–060 | Cross-domain identity, provenance/trust, capability mapping, no privilege escalation, workload identities, trust boundaries, delegation, revocation/expiry, privileged actions, trust matrix |
| X36.07 Runtime & Execution Environment Interoperability | X36-061–070 | Runtime prerequisites, ABI/calling conventions, process/sandbox, memory/files/IPC, WASM/native profiles, ATC-VM host, ATCLang artifact/runtime chain, Aurora agent/tool boundaries, service availability, runtime report |
| X36.08 Hardware & Platform Integration Profiles | X36-071–080 | Platform/CPU/memory/device/accelerator profiles, GPU/NPU, drivers/HAL, Secure Boot, firmware/boot protocols, GlobusOS installation, unsupported combinations, platform matrix |
| X36.09 Build, Artifact & Supply-Chain Integration | X36-081–090 | Build/artifact identity, source-to-output binding, hashes, signatures/provenance, toolchains, build features/reproducibility, SBOM, test linkage, artifact provenance |
| X36.10 Configuration & Environment Composition | X36-091–100 | Configuration profiles/schemas, required settings/dependencies/conflicts, secret references without disclosure, dev/test/prod alignment, secure defaults/fail-closed, environment drift, profile export |
| X36.11 End-to-End Integration Testing | X36-101–110 | Cross-system scenarios/call chains, provider-consumer contracts, cross-repo orchestration, real components vs test doubles, negative paths, recovery, Run/Job/Step/exit-code evidence, reproducible reports |
| X36.12 Cross-System Failure Isolation & Degradation | X36-111–120 | Failure domains/boundaries, timeouts/cancellation, circuit breakers, optional-service outage, safe degradation, recovery/state reconciliation, cascade prevention, authorized fallbacks, failure matrix |
| X36.13 Observability & Cross-System Correlation | X36-121–130 | Correlation/trace IDs, component/build-bound logs, cross-trust traces, error classes, interface/runtime metrics, test/deployment context, time conventions, telemetry redaction, alert correlation, evidence timeline |
| X36.14 Security & Policy Composition | X36-131–140 | Policy composition/conflicts, end-to-end least privilege, approvals for privileged actions, policy inheritance/boundaries, revocation/emergency stop, trust transitions, audit, fail-closed unknown state, policy evidence |
| X36.15 Performance & Capacity Across System Boundaries | X36-141–150 | End-to-end latency budgets, call-chain resource aggregation, redundant copies/buffering, backpressure, throughput/capacity, CPU/GPU/NPU paths, cold-start/recovery costs, bottlenecks, SLO comparisons, report |
| X36.16 Integration Lifecycle & Compatibility Evolution | X36-151–160 | Profile versioning, approved component combinations, pre-merge compatibility, stale contracts, migrations, backward-compatible upgrades, rollback compatibility, expiring exceptions, approvals/owners, lifecycle closure |
| X36.17 Conformance, Evidence & Architecture Governance | X36-161–170 | Normative criteria, all 17 sublayers, unique IDs, catalog reconciliation, evidence mapping, status classification, evidence freshness/exact commit, drift, auditable report, evidence-gated profile release |

## Proposed contract: `ATC-SYSTEM-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT-V1`

**Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`. This draft is not a substitute for canonical API, protocol, event, security or runtime standards, and is not normative until reviewed and formally registered in `atc-standards`.

```yaml
contract_id: ATC-SYSTEM-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT-V1
status: PROPOSED
verification: NOT_VERIFIED
architecture_layer: X36
architecture_id: ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X36-ECOSYSTEM-INTEGRATION-SYSTEM-COMPOSITION-END-TO-END-COMPATIBILITY

scope:
  - component_composition
  - dependency_validation
  - cross_repository_contract_mapping
  - end_to_end_compatibility
  - integration_evidence

identity:
  repository: required
  commit_sha: required
  source_path: required_when_applicable
  symbol: required_when_applicable
  blob_sha: required_when_available

component_contract:
  component_id: required
  interface_version: required
  dependencies: explicit
  capabilities: explicit
  trust_boundary: explicit

compatibility:
  api_schema_protocol: required
  runtime_platform_profile: required
  data_contract: required_when_applicable
  policy_contract: required

verification:
  test_run_id: required
  job_step_exit_code: required
  logs_or_artifacts: required
  artifact_hashes: required_when_artifacts_exist
  evidence_status:
    - MAPPED
    - IMPLEMENTED
    - VERIFIED
    - RESIDUAL
    - BLOCKED
    - UNRESOLVED
    - EXCLUDED

governance:
  unknown_critical_dependency: BLOCKED
  missing_required_evidence: NOT_VERIFIED
  duplicate_implementation: REVIEW_REQUIRED
  demo_repository_live_drift_gate: EXCLUDED
  merge_requires_exact_evidence: true
```

Before normative adoption, define field types, hash algorithms, error codes, signature/approval semantics and platform-specific mandatory fields.

## Canonical SSOT boundaries

| Area | Canonical responsibility | X36 role |
|---|---|---|
| Blockchain core | `a-townchain` | Reconcile integration contracts and system tests |
| ATC-VM | `a-townchain/components/vm` | Validate VM interfaces and host integration |
| Algorithm/consensus | `a-townchain/components/algorithm` | Validate dependencies and protocol boundaries |
| ShivaCore kernel | `globus-os/modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/` | Check kernel/OS boundaries and security assumptions |
| GlobusOS | `globus-os` | Validate platform, services, installation and runtime integration |
| ATCLang | Canonical implementation path must be verified | Reconcile compiler, artifact and runtime chain |
| Aurora AI | Canonical implementation path must be verified | Integrate agent, tool, policy and runtime contracts |
| Normative standards | `atc-standards` | Reference binding protocol/contract rules |
| Architecture/integration control | `a-townchain-ecosystem` | Catalog, dependency graph, evidence and drift checks only |

Verify concrete paths and ownership against current repository state before binding contracts. The ecosystem catalog must not host a second productive VM, kernel, algorithm, language or AI runtime implementation.

## Architecture invariants

1. One implementation per canonical SSOT; integration must not create parallel implementations.
2. Dependencies and integration behavior require explicit contracts.
3. Verification binds to exact full commit SHAs and uniquely identified artifacts.
4. Unknown critical dependencies block release/profile approval.
5. `IMPLEMENTED` and `VERIFIED` are distinct statuses.
6. Schema/API/data/runtime compatibility is checked before integration approval.
7. System composition cannot grant additional authority; least privilege holds end-to-end.
8. Optional-component failure must not destabilize the whole system in an uncontrolled way.
9. Evidence is reproducible and traceable to runs, jobs, steps, exit codes, logs and artifact hashes.
10. Missing/conflicting evidence remains `RESIDUAL`, `BLOCKED` or `UNRESOLVED`; it is not treated as success.
11. `demo-repository` is excluded from the live drift gate.
12. Green CI alone is not verification.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory components, repositories, canonical paths, contracts and existing evidence.
2. Reconcile SSOT ownership and dependency graph; identify forbidden duplicates.
3. Map APIs, data, identity, runtime and platform contracts.
4. Define and run provider-consumer, negative-path, recovery and end-to-end tests.
5. Bind evidence to exact commits, workflow runs/jobs/steps, exit codes, logs and artifact hashes.
6. Enable evidence-based release gates only after coverage and independent review.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 170 planned IDs are classified as `MAPPED`, `MISSING`, `UNRESOLVED` or `EXCLUDED`, with reasons and evidence.
- Every mapped implementation references the exact repository, full commit SHA, path, symbol/blob and supporting evidence.
- Only genuinely missing contracts are added to the catalog; canonical implementations are not duplicated.
- Proposed standards remain distinct from formally registered normative standards.
- End-to-end compatibility is demonstrated separately from manifest presence or green CI.
- Failure isolation, safe degradation, recovery and privilege boundaries have reproducible tests.
- Evidence includes Run → Job → Step, exit codes/logs and artifact hashes.
- No contract is promoted to `VERIFIED` without inspectable, matching evidence.

## Initial readiness checklist (0/10)

- [ ] Check X36 architecture ID and scope for duplicates in the catalog.
- [ ] Check uniqueness of all 17 sublayers and 170 contract IDs.
- [ ] Verify canonical repositories, paths and symbols.
- [ ] Reconcile SSOT/dependency graph against current repository state.
- [ ] Build contract and compatibility matrix.
- [ ] Reconcile API, data, identity and runtime contracts.
- [ ] Validate platform and installation profiles.
- [ ] Define and execute end-to-end and negative tests.
- [ ] Archive test runs, exit codes, logs and artifact hashes.
- [ ] Classify gaps and review evidence-based profile gate.

This checklist is tracking metadata only and does not itself verify repository state or CI.

## Current status

- Architecture: `PROPOSED`
- Verification: `NOT VERIFIED`
- Catalog intake: `NOT VERIFIED`
- Implementation: `UNRESOLVED`
- Planned sublayers: 17
- Planned function contracts: 170

Issue creation does not prove catalog integration, implementation or CI verification. First reconcile X36 against the current catalog and canonical repositories; add only genuinely missing contracts.
